title: Proactive capacity hedging and staged node replacement for zero-SLO perturbation
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: During planned maintenance (kernel/drivers/upgrades) or unscheduled host replacement, we observe transient latency/throughput regressions on Dedicated pools caused by KV-cache cold-starts, unbalanced slot handoffs, and synchronous drain policies. Objective: implement a proactive capacity hedging and staged node-replacement flow that guarantees throughput contracts during maintenance windows while minimizing cost and avoiding queue bloat.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Routine 1% maintenance on a 500-GPU pool must not cause tail latency violations beyond the configured SLO for more than 5 minutes in aggregate.
2) New staged node-replacement flow supports: preheated spare lanes, shadow-traffic cache warmup, admission control for long in-flight requests, and failback that restores previous capacity within 3 minutes.
3) Console shows per-pool hedging budget, active hedges, and expected extra cost estimate prior to window.
4) Automated rollouts use canary lane then bulk replacement with KV prewarm success metric >= 95% before shifting production routing.
5) Integration tests (CI) simulate drain + replace with synthetic workload and validate throughput contract adherence.</br>
tasks: Design: define hedging budget model (statistical headroom vs fixed spare lanes)
Runtime: implement 'spare lane' allocation and fast-preempt spin-up API
Runtime: KV cache snapshot/restore shim to support shadow prewarm
Control plane: staged-replacement orchestration with canary lane gating
Console: dashboard panel for hedging budget, projected cost, and live state
E2E: synthetic workload harness to validate SLO preservation
QA: chaos test for failure during prewarm and failback path
comments: 2026-02-21 - Kickoff: alignment with PM and Site Reliability. Decided to pursue a hybrid hedging model (preferred) that combines stateless spare lanes for short drains and probabilistic headroom for longer windows. Action: Marcus to prototype spare lane API.

2026-02-26 - Design review: Trade-offs discussed. Conservative approach (persistent spare lanes) increases cost but minimizes complexity and risk. Probabilistic approach reduces cost but requires better traffic forecasting. We agreed to implement persistent spare lanes configurable per-pool with an opt-in probabilistic hedging experiment. Review feedback: add KV-prewarm success metric and expose to console. @Sofia Gonzalez requested stricter rollbacks for canary failures.

2026-03-01 - Prototype update: spare-lane allocation implemented in runtime branch; initial KV snapshot API in GitHub PR #8765. Observed 40% faster warmup when playing prefix traces compared to cold-start. Next: integrate admission control to throttle new long-inflight tasks during cutover. @Nikhil Rao suggested adding tokenized throughput reservation to allow customers to buy-time for maintenance windows.

2026-03-05 - Ops simulation: ran staged replacement on a 300-GPU private pool using synthetic L1/L2 mixes. Canary succeeded; bulk shift triggered KV prewarm window and saw 98% warmup success before traffic cut. Minor bug: stale slot mapping caused a 200ms tail on one host — fixed in runtime PR #8792. Planning production pilot in one low-risk customer pool the week of 2026-03-22.
notes:
Implementation choices:
- We prioritize zero-SLO perturbation for P0 customers; hedging budget defaults to 5% spare lanes for P0 pools and is configurable.
- KV prewarm implemented via shadow-traffic playback using observed prefix traces; we will iterate on bandwidth and timeouts to balance cost.
- Admission control will reject/queue only new high-latency batch jobs but allow short interactive requests to flow.
Open questions: exact pricing model for tokenized throughput reservations, opt-in UX for customers, and KPIs for probabilistic hedging experiment.
